name: AdvancedEncryption.WE.Praxis.zeroTest_search_card_le
title: Search with zero tests only: each nontrivial affine test a t + b = 0 detects at most one candidate, so k tests cover at most k candidates
statement: Let K be a field, S a finite set of candidates t in K, and tests a finite family of pairs (a_i, b_i), none equal to (0, 0). Then the number of t in S for which some test satisfies a_i t + b_i = 0 is at most the number of tests. Reading: if the decryptor holds Lambda' = t* Psi with Psi != 0 and can only zero-test linear combinations a Lambda' + b Psi (no canonical names, so no baby-step giant-step), each zero test checks a single candidate value of t*, so a search over a range of size R needs about R tests. Used in note pq-we-praxis-bilinear-substitutes for name-free noisy encodings.
